vehicle.gvwr: Class 1: 6,000 lb or less (2,722 kg or less)

pids.0156: long term secondary O2 trim bank 1 (%)

signals.name: odometer
signals.verified: read against the dashboard one minute into a running log (142,934 mi), and again as +5 km over a 17-minute drive

signals.name: coolant temperature (SAE scale)
signals.verified: raw - 40, the SAE form. Against the legislated coolant PID: r=0.999, slope 0.979, offset +3.4 degC -- a DIFFERENT measuring point on the engine rather than a mirror of 0105, which is what the offset shows. Recorded as inferred only because the sample count behind the r was not preserved; the correlation itself is well above the 0.90 floor. Re-measured against this project's own warm-up log: r=+0.9966 over 19 samples. Above the 0.90 floor and below the 30-sample one, so it stays inferred rather than correlated -- only one road test here captured a warm-up, and it is 31 rows.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of the enhanced blocks

signals.name: oil temperature
signals.verified: value x 0.75 - 48, the community temperature form. Anchored against the legislated coolant PID rather than assumed, at r=0.9896 with zero lag. That establishes it is an engine temperature; that it is specifically the OIL temperature rests on the block it sits in and on 0x2244 reading as a temperature range throughout. Not swept at all until 2026-08-23. Re-measured here against the same warm-up log: r=+0.9803 over 19 samples. Same shortfall.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of 0x2258xx

signals.name: reference torque
signals.verified: raw x 0.1 gives 398.9 Nm, the stock N55 reference figure, which is the external check. NOT a constant: it moved between 3985 and 3989 counts within one drive, so it is a live baseline rather than a calibration value. 2258BA is expressed as a percentage of it, and horsepower as 2258BA x 224517 x rpm. Same tuning caveat as 2258BA: the convention transfers, the number may not.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of 0x2258xx

signals.name: coolant temperature (sensor value)
signals.verified: Mean 104.0 against a 103.8 anchor over 125 samples, r=0.973. A second coolant measuring point that agrees with the legislated PID and with 224300.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: rev limiter
signals.verified: Constant 6800. Confirmed because a wide-open-throttle pull reached exactly 6800 rpm -- the value the field holds is the value the engine stopped at, which is an external anchor rather than a correlation. Note the 7000 in the gauge profile's RPM row is the dial's full scale, not the limiter.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of the enhanced blocks

signals.name: unidentified — not engine load
signals.verified: Recorded here as engine load and that is probably wrong. The published map runs 4A49, 4A4A, GAP, 4A4C-4A4F as 'output ignition angle 0-5' -- 4A4B is a hole in the middle of a six-cylinder set. This project's own measurement already declined it: r=-0.19 against the legislated load PID. Worth testing as s16 x 0.1 degrees KW against 010E.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: vehicle speed
signals.verified: Mean 41.9 against a 43.1 anchor over 124 samples, r=0.699. Note OBDb disagrees with the published map on this identifier; this car sides with the map. Recorded as inferred rather than correlated: r=0.699 reflects a coarse 34 s row interval against a changing speed, not a weak identification; the means agree to 1.2 mph.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: operating hours counter
signals.verified: Reads 15,928,095 s = 4,424 hours. Against 142,934 recorded miles that is a 32.3 mph lifetime average, which is where a road car should sit.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: ambient temperature
signals.verified: Decodes within 0.2-1.0 degC of the ambient anchor on four of five distinct raw values; mean 25.2 against 26.3 over 124 samples. r is only 0.49 because ambient spans just 24-29.5 degC here -- the ABSOLUTE agreement is the evidence, not the correlation. Also explains why 225817 and 2258EB looked byte-identical over 1,427 rows: ambient barely moves. Recorded as inferred rather than correlated: ambient spans only 24-29.5 degC here, so r is meaningless; the absolute agreement is the evidence.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: coolant sensor signal voltage
signals.verified: r=-0.981 against coolant over 124 samples. An NTC thermistor's signal voltage MUST fall as temperature rises, so the sign is the confirmation -- this is the hardest of these rows to get right by accident.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: oil pressure
signals.verified: s16 x 1 hPa, ABSOLUTE. Reads 1000-1040 hPa with the engine stopped -- atmospheric, correct for oil pressure at rest -- and 2414-4528 hPa running, which is 2.4-4.5 bar absolute. The scale this project flagged as unverified is confirmed. Skipping the barometric subtraction is what made an earlier decode read ~15 psi high.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: ceramic temperature of the LSU
signals.verified: Reads 678-786 degC. A heated wideband lambda element is held near 780 degC, so the value identifies itself.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

signals.name: crank torque
signals.verified: Anchored on engine behaviour, three ways independent of scale: it collapses to zero on overrun, it peaks at 5940 rpm for power and 3800 rpm for torque -- the N55's published curve -- and it correlates r=+0.938 against MAF-derived power. Scale then pinned at 0.1 Nm/count from the DME's own calibration convention. Reported live as a percentage of 224517. The donor car is TUNED, so the magnitudes here are this vehicle's rather than a stock N55's; the 0.1 Nm/count convention is what transfers, and it should hold on any MEVD17.2.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of 0x2258xx. UNNAMED IN ALL SIX COMMUNITY BMW LISTS -- this is not a decode anyone published, it was worked out from the car.

signals.name: low-pressure fuel rail
signals.verified: 0x1A90 = 680.0 kPa = 6.8 bar, constant across five complete sweeps -- which is what a closed-loop regulated low-pressure fuel rail does. I previously recorded this as a second rev limiter because 0x1A90 is also 6800 and matched 224A2E. That was a unit collision between rpm counts and 0.1-kPa counts, not a shared value.
signals.source: cross-checked against a community-published N55 DME map (thesecretingredient.neocities.org/bmw/dme/n55, anonymous, no stated derivation) and CONFIRMED here against this car's own logs

source: obd-discover, 4 on-car capture(s) 2026-08; Mode-01 support scanned 2026-08-29
notes: 535i (F10). An earlier note here claimed 2258xx and 224Axx were absent from the community lists; that was WRONG -- they are the two best-covered blocks in the published N55 map, at 125 of 227 and 51 of 131. What survives is narrower and still true: 2258BA, 224517, 224303 and 224A2E appear in none of the N55, S55, B58, N63 or B48 maps. Enhanced Mode-22 reads in the 58xx block on the 7DF functional broadcast decode byte 0 only; a full u16 read there ingests NAK frames. That constraint comes from obd-gauge-cluster's profile and matters for anyone decoding 2258xx from a broadcast. 225817 and 2258EB were oil-temperature candidates in the 58xx block and are byte-identical to each other on 99.51% of 1,427 logged rows -- one signal under two identifiers, which is what makes them candidates rather than two findings. Horsepower on the dash is computed from 2258BA x 224517 x rpm; everything else shown there is standard Mode-01, not enhanced DIDs. 2258F3 turned out to be the low-pressure fuel rail, not a second limiter.

anchors.note: coolant; confirmed 0x2244 as a temperature block

addressing_detail.7DF: 42 PIDs — the functional broadcast, where everything above was found
addressing_detail.note: settled by the ECUs' own supported-PID bitmaps rather than by guessing headers

open_questions: 224303 and 224A4B promote to `correlated` given a cold-start log of 30+ samples. Only one road test here caught a warm-up and it yielded 19.
224A4B needs a DENSE log rather than a long one: load moves faster than the ~8 s row interval, so sparse sampling cannot confirm it.
2258BA wants MAF-derived power as its anchor, not rpm. Against rpm it scores r=+0.46 here, which says nothing -- torque is not a function of engine speed.
22586F's scale is unverified and needs a known-pressure anchor; no road test can supply one, so this wants a gauge or a spec figure at a known operating point.
2258F3 holds the limiter's value in all five sweeps but constants cannot be told apart by correlation. Distinguishing it from 224A2E needs a car with a different limiter.
225817 and 2258EB are one signal under two identifiers and neither is identified.
